title: Length-prefixed frame codec over a byte stream
premise: A service exchanges messages over a byte stream using a length-prefixed framing format, and the codec that turns a stream of bytes into discrete messages (and back) must be implemented from the stated wire spec.
spec: Implement encode(msg)->bytes and a streaming decoder feed(chunk)->list[msg]. Wire format: each frame is a 4-byte big-endian unsigned length N (of the payload only) followed by N payload bytes. The decoder is fed arbitrary chunk boundaries from the transport: a chunk may contain part of one frame, several whole frames, or a frame split across many chunks. feed must return exactly the frames now fully available, in order, buffering any partial remainder for the next call. A declared length exceeding MAX_FRAME (stated constant) must be rejected with a stated error before buffering the payload. encode/decode must round-trip for any payload including empty and MAX_FRAME-sized.
hardness_source: The difficulty is correct streaming state across chunk boundaries plus three interacting facets that a first-pass impl gets wrong: (1) reassembly of a frame split across multiple feed() calls; (2) draining multiple coalesced frames from one chunk; (3) bounded rejection of an oversized declared length WITHOUT first buffering N bytes (a naive impl reads N then checks). Applied domain knowledge: length-prefixed wire framing and incremental parser state.
adversarial_cases: Held-out conformance corpus fed with pathological chunkings the agent never sees: the 4-byte length header itself split across two chunks; a single chunk carrying 3.5 frames; an empty-payload frame between two full ones; an oversized-length frame that must be rejected at the header, before its (never-arriving) payload; a MAX_FRAME-sized frame delivered one byte per chunk. Grading feeds the SAME byte sequence under many random-but-fixed chunk splittings and requires identical decoded frame lists.
trap: Assuming one feed() call yields exactly one frame (read header, then read length bytes) — passes the visible single-frame examples, fails coalesced and split frames and buffers before the size check.
why_hard: A naive read-one-frame-per-chunk implementation passes the happy-path examples but fails held-out chunkings; correctness requires a persistent buffer, a header/payload state machine, and header-time size rejection, all interacting.
difficulty_summary: The agent must implement a streaming length-prefixed codec whose decoded output is invariant to chunk boundaries, drains coalesced frames, reassembles split frames, and rejects oversized frames at the header.
graded_on: Round-trip encode/decode on held-out payloads, and decode invariance across many fixed random chunk splittings of a held-out byte stream (identical ordered frame lists), plus oversized-length rejection observed before payload buffering.
capability_name: Build to spec under adversarial input

title: Arithmetic expression evaluator with precedence and error recovery
premise: A tool evaluates arithmetic expressions supplied as text, and the evaluator must be implemented from the stated grammar.
spec: Implement eval(text)->number|error for expressions over integers with + - * / and parentheses, unary minus, and standard precedence/associativity (*,/ bind tighter than +,-; left-associative; / is integer division truncating toward zero; division by zero is a stated recoverable error). Whitespace is insignificant. On a malformed expression, return a stated structured error naming the 0-based byte offset of the first offending token, and continue to accept subsequent well-formed calls (no crash, no persistent state).
hardness_source: Three interacting facets a first-pass impl gets wrong: (1) correct precedence AND left-associativity (naive left-to-right or naive recursive descent without precedence mis-evaluates 8-2*3 or 8/4/2); (2) unary minus disambiguated from binary minus by position; (3) error offsets that point at the FIRST offending token, exact byte offset, with recovery. Applied domain knowledge: precedence parsing (Pratt / precedence climbing) and tokenizer offset tracking.
adversarial_cases: Held-out expressions: nested unary minus (- -3), precedence chains (2+3*4-5), associativity (16/2/2, 16-2-2), parenthesized overrides, division-by-zero deep in a subexpression, and malformed inputs whose first error is mid-string (a bad token after several valid ones) requiring the exact offset. Grading uses expressions the agent never sees and checks both values and error offsets.
trap: Evaluating strictly left-to-right or hard-coding a few precedence cases — passes simple visible examples, fails associativity/precedence chains and offset-accurate errors.
why_hard: A naive evaluator passes trivial examples but fails precedence/associativity edge cases and exact error offsets; correctness needs a real precedence parser plus offset-tracking tokenizer, and the facets do not auto-satisfy each other.
difficulty_summary: The agent must implement a precedence-correct, associativity-correct integer expression evaluator with unary minus, truncating division, and offset-accurate recoverable errors.
graded_on: Values on held-out well-formed expressions (precedence, associativity, unary minus, integer division), stated errors with exact first-offending byte offset on held-out malformed expressions, and no persistent state across calls.
capability_name: Build to spec under adversarial input
